rationale: This is essentially an arithmetic blend of two archive signals (LowMarginInventoryBuild, fmb_tstat -4.47, and the much weaker LiquidityStrainedInventoryBuild, fmb_tstat -1.19) with the identical inventory-growth leg, so it is a cosmetic averaging that most likely dilutes the stronger margin conditioner rather than a new mechanism.

Replacing inventory growth with an inventory-intensity ramp is a genuine change to the investment leg motivated by the archive's finding that ACCEL improved the capex family (ls_talpha -3.95 vs -2.21), though the low-gross-profitability leg means part of any result will simply reload on the Novy-Marx profitability anomaly.

This is CashWeakCapexAcceleration with only the conditioning variable swapped from cash-flow quality to gross margin — an incremental one-leg substitution rather than the substantively different construction the objective calls for, and the substituted leg is itself a well-known standalone anomaly.

The three-way rank product is dominated by the joint tail and, more importantly, the two active components (share issuance and low profitability) are among the most heavily documented published anomalies, so a negative result would largely be a rediscovery rather than evidence for the cash-hoarding channel.

The intangible-build leg is the least-explored component and the hypothesis matches the expression's direction, but the triple rank product will thin an already low-coverage sample (LowProfitIntangibleBuild was 0.117) and overlaps meaningfully with the archived ExternallyFundedCashFlowWeakExpansion, so it needs to beat that benchmark rather than merely be significant.

A plain product of two published anomalies — the hiring-rate/employment-growth effect (Belo-Lin-Bazdresch) and reversed gross profitability (Novy-Marx) — with no conditioning structure beyond their interaction, and the archive's two prior hiring conditionings both failed (fmb_tstat 0.05 and -1.64), making this both derivative and unpromising.
